description: When the kidneys are not working well, metformin can build up and raise the risk of a rare but serious condition called lactic acidosis.
source: FDA label: metformin HCl tablets, Boxed Warning, §4, §8.7

description: Ibuprofen can reduce blood flow to the kidneys and make kidney problems worse.
source: FDA label: ibuprofen tablets Rx (Precautions, Drug Interactions); AGS Beers Criteria 2023 Table 6

description: Naproxen can reduce blood flow to the kidneys and make kidney problems worse.
source: FDA label: naproxen tablets §5.6, §8.5, §8.7; AGS Beers Criteria 2023 Table 6

description: Simvastatin should not be used in active or severe liver disease, and needs caution with other liver problems, because it can further affect the liver.
source: FDA label: Zocor (simvastatin) §4; UK SmPC: Simvastatin 20 mg §4.3

description: Liver disease can make paracetamol more likely to cause liver harm.
source: UK SmPC: Paracetamol 500 mg Tablets (Zentiva) §4.4; FDA label: Ofirmev (acetaminophen) §5.1

description: In older adults, oxybutynin is more likely to cause confusion, constipation and other side effects.
source: FDA label: oxybutynin chloride tablets (Precautions, Geriatric Use); AGS Beers Criteria 2023 Table 7

description: With reduced kidney function, spironolactone can cause high potassium levels.
source: FDA label: Aldactone (spironolactone) §5.1, §8.5, §8.6; AGS Beers Criteria 2023 Table 6

description: Children and teenagers are more likely to get movement-related side effects from metoclopramide.
source: FDA label: Reglan (metoclopramide) §5.2, §8.4; EMA press release 2013-07-26
